Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating preference timescales. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) uses separate long/short self-attention networks with temporal embeddings. [Hierarchical long/short preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) represents older history with multiple interest vectors, matches these against current short-term intent, and fuses them through time encoding. The useful principle: retrieve relevant older preferences rather than average all history into one broad vector.

Repetition and noise deserve separate treatment. [LSIDN (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) gives long/short branches different encoders and denoising strategies. [GDA-REIM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026001838) combines differential attention with repetition–exploration scoring and an intent-discrimination loss. Its historical-item pointer is relevant when repeat consumption is allowed; for unseen-item recommendations, recurring interests should instead guide scores toward related unseen items. [Dual-Interest Multi-Granular SSM (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) separates stable-history aggregation from local intent, using interaction gaps to modulate short-term state evolution.

Practical synthesis, rather than a directly validated architecture: retain SASRec for recent intent; add a small bank of pooled historical interests and a recurrence-sensitive branch using learned item similarities. Fuse branch scores with a gate conditioned on recent features, elapsed gaps, and history length. Compare fixed mixing against learned gating, then add timestamp decay and multiple historical vectors separately. This offers a lightweight way to test whether stale affinities are suppressing current intent; the cited results do not establish gains on the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

---

Multi-negative training is a strong candidate, but negative count and loss calibration should be tested separately. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence from sampled BCE and combines more negatives with generalized BCE. Sampled softmax provides another efficient objective. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional sampling correction mishandles the always-present positive; its refined formulation reports improvements over standard logQ correction. This matters particularly for popularity-biased in-batch negatives; sampling correction does not itself resolve false negatives.

Adaptive mining should balance informativeness against false-negative risk. [CATS (2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) combines item clustering with Thompson sampling, progressively reducing sampling from the positive item’s cluster while exploring neighboring clusters and the remaining catalog. Its cluster-based false-negative assumption is a heuristic, not an observed label. Practical RecHarness experiment proposal: compare uniform multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE first, then add a small stochastic hard-negative component mined from a bounded candidate pool after warm-up. Exclude padding, the target, and known training positives; retain random negatives and avoid hardest-only selection. Sweep modest negative counts, such as 16/64/128, and hard-negative fractions under equal GPU budgets. These settings are proposed ablations, not published optima. Select using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; inspect Electronics margins and category regressions without assuming published gains transfer to this benchmark.

---

Recent work supports combining item text with behavioral signals, but much of it requires pretrained language models. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) adds BERT-derived titles, descriptions and reviews to SASRec; its strongest textual contribution came from reviews, unavailable here. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns description embeddings with collaborative signals through contrastive learning, highlighting that semantic similarity alone can miss behavioral relationships. Neither provides direct evidence for an entirely scratch-trained text encoder under this benchmark’s constraints.

Candidate-conditioned history matching is a promising architectural direction. [Interaction Fidelity Attention (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09742) models candidate-to-history cross-attention and processes candidates jointly using linear attention to reduce computational cost. An adaptation worth testing: preserve SASRec’s sequential score, then add a candidate-conditioned attention score over historical items using locally trained title/description token embeddings. Preserve numbers, units, model identifiers and format tokens; compare simple token pooling against a small text encoder. These are proposed adaptations, not established improvements for the four target datasets.

Distinguishing broad content similarity from specification compatibility requires explicit evidence. Token overlap can identify shared formats or model numbers, but cannot establish accessory fit or interoperability when metadata omits those facts. Treat missing specifications as unknown, avoid fabricated compatibility labels, and learn any text contribution from training interactions. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec models next-item preference using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Candidate scores are dot products between the final sequence representation and shared item embeddings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
